name: Richmond International Airport
before:
Central Virginia's airport, about 7 miles south east of downtown Richmond in Sandston, and third busiest in the state behind the two Washington airports. Seven carriers fly non-stop to 26 destinations.

It has been rebuilt twice this century. A complete redesign announced in 2005 took the terminal from a single storey with 12 gates to a two level building with upper level departures and lower level arrivals, 22 gates, a new control tower and parking for 10,500. A second expansion ran from late 2018 to 2021, adding gates to the A Concourse and widening the Concourse B security area from four lanes to six.

International flying is seasonal and works through gate B15, which reopened for Cancun, Toronto and Punta Cana.

The airport covers 2,500 acres and is a joint civil and military site, taking in the former Air National Guard station now used by the US Army Reserve and Virginia Army National Guard.

It is owned and run by the Capital Region Airport Commission, set up in 1975 and answerable to Richmond and three surrounding counties.
after:
Central Virginia's airport, a short drive south east of downtown Richmond in Henrico County, and third busiest in the state behind the two Washington airports. The airport lists nine airlines, with nonstop flights to major US cities and connections beyond.

A renovation completed in 2007 gave the terminal two levels, with departures upstairs and arrivals below. Each of the two concourses, A and B, has its own security checkpoint. A $253 million project will merge them into one, letting passengers move freely between concourses; work is due to begin in late 2026.

Breeze Airways plans twice-weekly seasonal flights to Cancún from 8 January 2027.

It is owned and run by the Capital Region Airport Commission, set up in 1975 and answerable to the City of Richmond and the counties of Chesterfield, Hanover and Henrico. Military aircraft use the airport too.

claims.claim: about 4.9 million passengers in 2025
claims.note: New to the text, as the answer to how busy it is, replacing the stale carrier and destination counts. TOTAL passengers, arriving plus departing: the operator's December 2025 report gives 4,922,994 for calendar 2025, up 0.8 per cent on 4,884,093 in 2024 (2,464,795 enplaned). The FAA's preliminary CY2025 table counts 2,481,863 enplanements (boardings only, about half of total passengers), which is consistent. The operator also reports a record 4.96 million for its fiscal year to June 2026 (release of 29 July 2026); not used, as no second source was saved for it.

claims.note: Replaces 'Seven carriers fly non-stop to 26 destinations', which is out of date. The operator's live airline page names nine: Allegiant, American, Breeze, Delta, Frontier, JetBlue, Southwest, Sun Country and United. It reflects Spirit's shutdown on 2 May 2026 (the operator's release of that day). An attributed statement, as for Austin and Timisoara: no second source for the count could be read (the Bureau of Transportation Statistics page needs a form post, Visit Richmond and Breeze answered 403, BermudAir 502). The operator's 'About' paragraph still lists BermudAir and Spirit, so it is older than the airline page. BizSense reported a BermudAir route to Bermuda in 2025; whether it still runs could not be confirmed, so the text does not mention it. Worth Andy's eye.

claims.claim: about 7 miles from downtown
claims.why: The sources do not agree on the figure: Wikipedia says about 7 miles (11 km); the operator's field information and its annual reports for 2021 and 2024 say 6 miles east of downtown; the FAA record says 6 nautical miles (about 6.9 statute miles). The coordinates give 8.4 miles in a straight line from the GeoNames centre. Figure dropped, direction kept, and 'a short drive' added from two sources.

claims.claim: in Sandston
claims.why: Only Wikipedia places it in Sandston; the FAA's CY2025 table gives its city as Highland Springs, and the operator and the FAA record give a Richmond postal address. Softened to Henrico County, which every source gives.

claims.claim: seven carriers to 26 destinations
claims.wasBefore: Seven carriers fly non-stop to 26 destinations.
claims.why: Out of date. The operator's live airline page now lists nine airlines, given as the airport's own statement; no current destination count was found.

claims.claim: rebuilt twice this century
claims.wasBefore: It has been rebuilt twice this century.
claims.why: Framing that undercounts: the operator's timeline lists a Concourse B expansion (2002), a new control tower (2004), the terminal renovation (2007), a garage extension (2010) and a Concourse A extension (from 2018). The 2007 renovation is kept.

claims.claim: redesign announced in 2005
claims.why: The 2005 announcement rests on Wikipedia alone; the 2007 completion is kept with two sources.

claims.claim: from a single storey with 12 gates to 22 gates
claims.wasBefore: took the terminal from a single storey with 12 gates
claims.why: Contradicted by the operator's history: a 1995 expansion at Concourse A increased the number of gates to 14, and a 2002 Concourse B expansion was a 50 per cent increase in gates, both before 2005. The 22-gate figure rests on Wikipedia alone.

claims.claim: 22 gates
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and inconsistent with the operator's history (see above). The operator's annual reports give 28 gates since 2021.

claims.claim: a new control tower as part of the 2005 redesign
claims.why: The operator dates the new air traffic control tower to 2004 (dedicated by the FAA), before the 2005 announcement it is attached to here.

claims.claim: parking for 10,500
claims.why: The operator gives 10,000 on-site spaces after the 2010 garage extension; Wikipedia gives 10,500. Disputed, and new parking decks are being planned (BizSense, December 2025).

claims.claim: second expansion late 2018 to 2021 adding gates to Concourse A
claims.wasBefore: A second expansion ran from late 2018 to 2021, adding gates to the A Concourse
claims.why: The start is confirmed (Wikipedia: late 2018; operator: a $28 million, six-gate extension of Concourse A in 2018), but the 2021 finish rests on Wikipedia alone and the history matters less to an agent than the checkpoint change now coming. Dropped to keep the text under 150 words.

claims.claim: Concourse B security widened from four lanes to six
claims.wasBefore: widening the Concourse B security area from four lanes to six
claims.why: Contradicted: BizSense (26 November 2025) says each existing checkpoint has four lanes. The operator's 2021 report confirms a Concourse B checkpoint widening project, but not six lanes. Replaced by the current two-checkpoint layout and the merger planned.

claims.claim: international flights through gate B15 to Cancun, Toronto and Punta Cana
claims.wasBefore: International flying is seasonal and works through gate B15, which reopened for Cancun, Toronto and Punta Cana.
claims.why: Out of date. In May 2026 the airport and Breeze both said Richmond had had no nonstop flight to Cancún for more than a decade; Air Canada's Toronto service dates from 2008 and Air Canada is not on the operator's airline list; B15 rests on Wikipedia alone. Replaced by the Breeze Cancún route due in January 2027.

claims.claim: 2,500 acres
claims.why: Disputed: the FAA record and Wikipedia give 2,500 acres, while the operator's annual reports (2021 and 2024) say the airport owns 3,078 acres.

claims.claim: joint civil and military site with the former ANG station used by the Army Reserve and Virginia Army National Guard
claims.wasBefore: is a joint civil and military site, taking in the former Air National Guard station now used by the US Army Reserve and Virginia Army National Guard
claims.why: The units and the transfer of the station rest on Wikipedia alone: the Virginia National Guard's site failed at the proxy (tunnel refused) and was not retried. Softened to military aircraft using the airport, which the operator's figures and the FAA record support.

claims.claim: answerable to Richmond and three surrounding counties (old wording)
claims.wasBefore: answerable to Richmond and three surrounding counties
claims.why: Reworded with the counties named. 'Surrounding' is a description neither source uses; the operator calls them the four Richmond-area jurisdictions.
